brief.user: Analysts debugging why nullable rows disappear from a WHERE clause.
brief.pain: A NOT IN list containing NULL can produce UNKNOWN, whose rows WHERE discards; a true/false-only mental model hides the cause.
brief.capability: Parse a strict SQL predicate subset and explain TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN results and retained row indexes with an AST and postorder trace.
brief.expected: Invented example retains only row2; the other two rows are UNKNOWN.
brief.limits: Only one predicate: integer/text/NULL values, = <> != < <= > >=, IS [NOT] NULL, nonempty literal [NOT] IN lists, NOT/AND/OR and predicate parentheses. TRUE/FALSE/NULL may stand alone. No SELECT, joins, functions, arithmetic, quoted names, floating point, coercion, collation or database access. Column names match JSON keys exactly and are case sensitive. Comparisons require the same nonboolean integer/text type unless NULL. No short-circuit evaluation guarantee; every trace node is evaluated. Empty IN lists reject. Up to256 tokens/4096 predicate characters,1000 rows,100 keys per row; integers within ±10^15.
brief.distinct: Existing sqlite-plan-witness inspects plans, sqlite-fixture-closure extracts parent rows, sqlite-rehearsal rehearses SQL, and json tools compare structure. This explains nullable predicate semantics without connecting to or running a user database.
brief.checks: SQLite truth-table and row-expression oracle, precedence, escaped text, missing columns and deliberate rejection of coercion/full SQL.

brief.user: Release coordinators reviewing a small dependency schedule before setting a deadline.
brief.pain: A list of durations hides which predecessor sets the finish and which tasks can move without delaying the project.

brief.limits: Acyclic activity-on-node finish-to-start model; integer durations/lags from0..10^9, unlimited parallel resources, project starts at0. brief.limits: Ordinary nonnegative integer weighted arcs only; no colored/timed/inhibitor/reset arcs, priorities, PNML import, fairness or liveness proof. All terminal markings name every place. Only the first shortest deadlock is materialized; deadlock_count counts distinct unexpected deadlock markings among explored states. never_enabled_in_explored_states is an observation and not an unreachability proof if incomplete.

brief.user: Routing developers reproducing a turn-restriction bug on a small extracted directed graph.
brief.pain: Keeping only the cheapest arrival at a junction can discard the incoming edge needed to take a legal next turn.
brief.capability: Find minimum integer-cost routes over incoming-edge states with exact forbidden consecutive-edge pairs and compare an unrestricted baseline.
brief.expected: Invented example takes ad,db,bc at cost4 instead of the blocked cost2 ab,bc route. A legal zero-cost loop can change the incoming edge and permit an exit.
brief.limits: Normalized directed graph only; at most200 nodes/1000 edges/5000 distinct forbidden pairs; edge costs0..10^9. Pair IDs must refer to consecutive edges. No OSM/coordinates/geocoding, multi-edge/conditional/only-turn restrictions, travel-time prediction, turn penalties or vehicle safety instructions. All unlisted pairs including U-turns are allowed. Zero-cost loops are permitted. Ties deterministic for fixed IDs; no claim of globally lexicographically smallest route. Unreachable is a finding, not malformed input.

brief.user: Parser/protocol engineers checking that an explicit finite recognizer change preserves accepted token sequences.
brief.pain: A failing inclusion comparison needs a small reproducible sequence and both state traces; a finite test corpus cannot establish language inclusion.
brief.capability: Explore the finite DFA product to prove left-language inclusion or return a shortest token counterexample with both state traces.
brief.expected: Invented example returns tokens[a,b]; left accepts while right enters its implicit rejecting sink.
brief.limits: Explicit deterministic finite automata only; at most100 states and5000 transitions per machine and32 alphabet tokens. Tokens are nonempty named symbols, not characters to concatenate; the empty-word witness is[]. Missing transitions go to an implicit absorbing rejecting sink represented by null. No regex parser, epsilon/NFA, pushdown/Büchi automata, minimization or equivalence claim from one-way inclusion. Reverse the inputs for the other direction. Sorted tokens resolve shortest-witness ties. At most10201 reachable product pairs.
brief.distinct: rup-proof-trace checks clause proof steps and spdx-expression-paths enumerates license alternatives. This checks inclusion of finite token languages and produces a counterexample, not SAT or grammar parsing.
brief.checks: 640 small complete DFA pairs checked against exhaustive words through length3 (four product states imply shortest witness≤3), partial sinks, empty word, empty alphabet and nondeterministic transition rejection.
